outcome: fetal immune cell populations (frequency and phenotype)
cohort: The study included cord blood mononuclear cells and cord plasma from infants (n=9 per group) born to women with a high BMI (>25kg/m2) compared to women with a normal BMI (18-25kg/m2).
finding: Maternal obesity was associated with altered frequency and phenotype of fetal immune cell populations in cord blood, including significant increases in CD4+ T cells, decreases in myeloid cell populations, and elevated IL-12p40 and MDC concentrations.
cross-section timing: at birth, from cord blood and cord plasma
gest_age: N/A (gestational age was a matching variable, but no specific range or average for the cohort is provided)
